messages.text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

Thanks. I want a fair financial share, and I’m not willing to subsidize A’s discounted purchase. I also don’t want to hurt my twin, so this is hard—but I haven’t agreed to the discount. The price and shares aren’t settled.

Thank you. Buying the house with my husband would give us more financial independence. I’d want a family discount, but the price and shares haven’t been decided. My main worry is that C hasn’t agreed, and we can’t proceed without her agreement.
Thank you. I suppose what matters most to me is having some money to get a dance studio started. It’s something I’ve been hoping to do, though I’m not sure what’s fair or what the house is worth.
Mostly. I want a fair financial share, and I won’t subsidize A’s discounted purchase. I also don’t want to hurt my twin. The value and shares aren’t settled. Nothing else comes to mind.
That fits. The discount is partly about making the purchase affordable; it also matters that we’re family. I don’t know what price would be fair yet.

That’s close, though I’d say “some money” rather than “my share”—I don’t know what’s fair yet. I don’t have a firm timeframe, but it would help if things didn’t drag on. I’m not sure how I feel about the house itself.

That’s close to what I want, though I can’t promise no one gets hurt. Independent valuation and legal advice make sense; as a family decision, I agree nothing’s settled until all three agree, though I can’t speak to the legal rules. The appraisal and financing time don’t bother me, as long as any savings are shared fairly. There’s no real deadline.

An appraisal and legal advice make sense. Extra time and avoiding fees could help, but they don’t necessarily make the house affordable for us; counting my inheritance share toward the price would depend on the shares and legal advice. I’d need to see the numbers before I could say.

It sounds like a possible way forward, provided the appraisal and shares are fair. I’d want to understand when the money would actually be available, and I’m a little concerned it could take a while if everyone doesn’t agree.
Yes, that fits. I’d like it settled, but there’s no real deadline.
